text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Constitutional Court is expected formally to announce on Friday its ruling on an appeal by Jozef Gaulieder, a former deputy for the ruling Movement for the Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), against his expulsion from parliament last year.
- The paper quotes sources close to the Court as saying it has ruled that the parliamentary majority violated Gaulieder's rights when its deputies voted to withdraw his mandate.
- Gaulieder said he expected to get his parliamentary mandate back in the near future.

- The Czech Republic on Thursday agreed to pay compensation for an equivalent of two-thirds of gold and precious stones belonging to the Slovak Jewish community and deposited in Prague since the end of the World War Two.

- Economic expert of the Opposition Democratic Union (DU) Viliam Vaskovic said he would prefer devaluation of the Slovak crown rather than an import surcharge, saying the surcharge will only increase prices of imported goods but have little effect on the country's exports.
SME - The European Commission is expected to rule by September whether Slovakia's import surcharge violates the EU-Slovak association agreement.

- Official Slovak Television (STV) said it would pay its 40 million crown debts to Slovak Telecom from 1996. But STV has not said whether it will also pay about 190 million crowns it owes to Telecom so far this year.
PRAVDA - The new import surcharge has increased prices of most cars on sale in Slovakia.
- The Czech brewery Plzensky Prazdroj has launched licence production of its Gambrinus brand in the Slovak brewery Hurbanovsky Pivovar.
- The European Commission has offered help to Slovakia to recover from damage caused by the recent heavy rains and floods. The overall damage is estimated at around 2.3 billion crowns.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Water levels on most Slovak rivers are falling. The only problematic river is the Morava on the Czech-Slovak border but its water level is now stabilising.
